commits.message:
Remove milestone labels, history narration and code kept for past designs

Comments, test titles, messages, docs and skills state the rule as it is:
issue numbers, goal and phase labels, ruling labels and accounts of what
the code used to do are gone. File names and identifiers that carried a
label are renamed after what they do.

Code that existed only for a delivered milestone or a past shape is
deleted rather than renamed: the journal kill-recovery harness, the
isolated-chain bootstrap scripts, the phase stress gates and their knobs,
the lettered benchmarks, the ledger-store exit benchmarks, retired CLI
routes and environment-variable guards, one-time table renames, the
migration_version column, unused submit result types, and on-chain
library functions reached only by their own tests.

Every validator keeps its hash and size.

Decide the import checker's deadline tests by a clock the test sets

The late-verdict and saturated-admission tests took a deadline from
`Date.now()`, waited for it on a timer, and then expected the checker,
which reads the wall clock, to have seen it pass. A timer runs on the
monotonic clock. When the wall clock was stepped backward during the wait,
the checker was still short of the deadline at the assertion, and the
missed alarm was absent (`expected [] to deeply equal [...]` at
import-check.late-verdicts.test.ts:151 and
import-check.saturation.test.ts:128).

The saturation test also left its sweep loop running when an assertion
threw. The loop then expired the next test's entry before that test swept,
which is the second failure the same runs show (line 213).

The tests now set the checker's time themselves:

- The late verdict comes from the scripted evaluator, whose run takes the
  test clock from before the deadline to exactly the deadline.
- The saturated pass and its sweeps run on one clock the test sets, with
  real sleeps because the pass waits on a real pool. The test waits for
  the run to be asked for and for admission to finish seven more runs
  after that, then sweeps one millisecond before the deadline (no alarm),
  at it (the alarm) and after it (not again). The pass is settled before
  the test ends, whatever failed.
- The entry "already past its deadline" is an hour past it, as the entries
  not yet due in these suites are an hour ahead.

These tests no longer sleep, and the two files run in about 6 s where
they took about 10 s.

On the machine the failures came from, the kernel log records the wall
clock jumping backward, and every recorded failure of these tests sits
in a run whose log timestamps go backward, in all but one of them by 1.7
to 2.1 s about every 30 s; no run with a steady clock failed. With
`Date.now` replaced in the setup file by a clock that steps back 700 ms
every second (a temporary edit), the old tests failed at the three
assertions above (4 of 9 tests) and the new ones passed 20 runs of 20;
they also passed 20 of 20 on the plain clock. Each of these changes to
checker.ts turns them red: `>=` to `>` on the verdict's deadline check,
`<=` to `<` on the sweep's, and dropping the raised-once guard in
`raiseMissed`.

Install the ledger in the test fixtures that ingest events without a node

A node gives no L1 event a row before its ledger is installed. Four test
files drive event ingestion without starting a node and never installed
one, so their deposits and forced orders got no row. Midgard Node CI
failed on a218a1df4 with six tests in these files.

- `deposit-flow-emulator-shared.ts`: an unowned fixture starts its native
  owner, whose start is the install, before each event ingestion. It was
  started by the first commit worker run, after the first ingestion. Fixes
  `da-bond-pool-bootstrap-emulator` and
  `state-queue-node-floor-challenge-emulator`.
- `forced-order-carriage-emulator.test.ts` and one test of
  `history-commit-window.test.ts` install the empty ledger in their setup.

Test files only; no source change.

Verified (rerun here):
- The four files: 16 passed, 0 failed.
- The 28 test files that import an edited file, directly or through
  another fixture: 50 passed, 0 failed.
- The files `contrib test --related` reaches from every source file this
  branch changed: 238 passed in 34 files.
- tsc --noEmit for midgard-node; eslint and prettier on the three files.

Not verified:
- The whole node suite locally. CI ran it on a218a1df4, where only these
  six tests failed.

Let the acceptance settlement drill outwait and recognise a settlement

The acceptance arms kill-node-on-settlement before the withdrawals phase
submits its orders and gave it 1200 s. On the devnet profile a withdrawal's
settlement starts no sooner than the event wait (300 s) and block maturity
(900 s) after its order, so the wait always ended first: on a live stack
the first settlement transaction appeared 1348 s after arming. The wait is
now the profile's event wait and block maturity plus 25 minutes.

The trigger also listed two details the node stopped reporting in
bc56f0822, and not the one it reports while a settlement transaction is in
a block short of confirmation depth. Four of eleven settlement
transactions on that stack went from checkpointed to landed with no
journaled report between. The node's two wordings now live in
settlement.attempt-detail.ts, and the catalogue test builds its status
bodies from them, so a reworded detail fails the test.

Red before the fix (tests/devnet-stack-chaos.test.ts, 6 passed, 2 failed):
  recognises each targeted moment from the node's status bodies
    expected [ ...(2) ] to deeply equal [ ...(2) ]
    (the landed detail, false against true)
  lets the acceptance wait past the earliest a withdrawal's settlement can
  start
    expected 1200000 to be greater than 1200000

Correct the retention rationale in decision record 0002

The parameter table said parties replay retained payloads from genesis. A
joining node or watcher now replays only the blocks above the confirmed
state; the 120 days stay as set.

Not verified: no doc check beyond prettier was run for this commit.

Remove the late-join limit from the docs

A node with an empty database now takes the confirmed ledger from a node
of the deployment, and a watcher already did. The readiness, security,
threat-model and parameters pages said every party replays from genesis
and that no state snapshot exists; they now say what a joining node or
watcher does and what it needs (one node serving the ledger, and the
retained payloads above the confirmed state).

The stack and e2e pages keep their attach-before-the-first-block flow and
say that joining after a merged block has not been run through the
harness.

Not verified: no doc check or preflight was run for this commit.

Start a node with no ledger from a peer's snapshot of the confirmed head

A node with no ledger stamp started only on a queue with no block. On any
other queue its first recompute failed with a hold that is not retried and
startup exited. It now takes in the ledger at the landed queue's confirmed
header H, whose post-state UTxO root is R, and syncs forward from there.

The take-in (`services/ledger-snapshot-start.ts`), run where the native
owner is initialized:

- R the empty ledger's root: the empty ledger, also when unmerged blocks
  sit above the confirmed head; landed-block processing replays them.
- Otherwise the peers in the new `LEDGER_SNAPSHOT_PEERS` (libp2p
  multiaddrs ending in `/p2p/<peer id>`) are asked in order for R over
  `ledger-snapshot`, from the node's DA libp2p host. The stream is staged
  in `node_ledger_snapshot_staging` and fed to the ledger store's `admit`,
  which checks it against R. A peer whose stream fails the check is not
  asked again by the process; a peer that does not serve R is asked again
  on the next attempt.
- With no peer serving, the node stays up and holds the new readiness
  reason `ledger_snapshot_pending`, retried without a deadline.
- One transaction installs it: the staged rows become `confirmed_ledger`
  and `mempool_ledger`, the frontier is set to (H, R), the ledger is
  stamped at R and the anchor is recorded. The stamp is the commit point:
  a start with no stamp empties the staging table and takes the ledger in
  again.

Every node now records an anchor, so the event rule reads one fact:
`givesNoRow` gives no row to any L1 event before the install, and after it
to none included at or before the anchor's end time. Landed-block
processing does nothing before the install.

Deleted, superseded by the install:

- the genesis-only admit in `native-mpf-startup.ts`, its two refusals
  ("requires the authenticated clean state queue", "Stale native ledger
  store") and `writeGenesisLedger`;
- `bootstrapFrontier`, the `genesis` port and the no-frontier hold: the
  install always sets the frontier. Test fixtures install through
  `takeInLedger` (`tests/helpers/ledger-install.ts`);
- `tests/landed-blocks-bootstrap-frontier.test.ts` and the two stale-store
  stages of `native-mpf-startup-emulator.test.ts`, which tested the
  deleted behaviour.

No on-chain change and no wire change.

Tests added: the install in one transaction, a wrong first peer refused
and the second used, pending then success, a crash between `admit` and the
install finished by the next start (`ledger-snapshot-take-in.test.ts`);
the node's configured peers dialed over real libp2p against a node's
retained-payload server (`ledger-snapshot-peers.test.ts`); a merge that
lands during the transfer folded from the queue history
(`confirmed-ledger-behind-recovery.test.ts`); and, through the production
lifecycle, an unmerged deployment starting empty, a merged one starting
from a peer after a pending ask, a deposit at or below the anchor given no
row and spendable once, a deposit above it taken by the node's next block,
the anchor's merge rolled back and landed again, and a block committed on
the tail (`ledger-snapshot-start-emulator.test.ts`).

Verified by the implementing and review runs, not rerun here:
- 75 midgard-node test files covering every touched test and fixture user:
  440 passed, 2 failed, both in tests/import-check.saturation.test.ts,
  which this change does not reach and which passed alone (4 of 4).
- Each new behaviour test seen red on a mutant of the code it covers,
  except the two deposit assertions added last: their mutants fail the
  test earlier than the new lines.
- tsc --noEmit for midgard-node; eslint and prettier on the changed files;
  contrib boundary --package midgard-node.

Not verified:
- Two node processes, a devnet or Preprod.
- A request in flight is not aborted on shutdown: the node's libp2p
  request takes no abort signal, so it ends at the per-request timeout.
- Preflight.

Name files and tests for what they do, and delete one-time goal scripts

- Files, constants and Aiken test modules named after an issue, goal
  or phase label are named for their purpose. Markdown docs, skills
  and the remaining code comments state the rule instead of citing a
  label. Decision records keep their identifiers.
- The node creates the follower's tables in the same transaction as
  the rest of its schema, so they are always present: the
  `landed_block_follower_schema_missing` hold and the table probes
  behind it are gone. The commit test fakes share one helper that
  models a complete, empty database.
- One-time capture and benchmark scripts with no caller are gone: the
  phase4 environment and slot-config captures, the phase1 query-write
  and group-commit benchmarks, the chunk128 candidate bench entry and
  the 10k smoke entry, whose test runs in the joined DA suite.
- The retained-DA boundary corpus check is
  `test:retained-da-boundary-corpus`.
- Naming guide: labels go in commit messages and decision records,
  never in names, comments, test titles or messages.

Give the devnet node read budgets the acceptance drills fit in

An armed acceptance phase drill reads its trigger every 10 ms. The devnet
node ran with the public rate limits (10 reads and 5 health reads a second
for one client), and the controller, its drills and the CLIs are one
loopback client. The node therefore refused most of the drill's reads and
the journey's own: /tx-status answered 429 with a JSON body, which the
journey read as "not committed yet".

Seen on a fresh devnet stack (campaign acceptance-user-cli-2, 2026-11-25):
the node committed transfers T1-T3 and their block landed six seconds after
they were submitted, yet the journey reported "still waiting for L2 tx ...
to be committed (node ready)" for 19 minutes, and kill-node-on-admission
ended with 'trigger "durable admission backlog > 0" did not hold within
1200 s'. The backlog was above zero for 37 ms. On that stack, 60 reads of
/pipeline-status in a row got 30 answers and then 429s, and /tx-status
answered 429 with them. The 10 ms interval dates from 2026-10-04; the rate
limits from 2026-10-26.

- The devnet node's environment raises the read and health budgets
  (HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_READ, HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_HEALTH). Every other class keeps
  its default.
- The journey treats a 429 as an unanswered read and names it in its
  reports, like a 5xx, instead of reading the refusal's body as a status.
- The interval has a name, ACCEPTANCE_TRIGGER_POLL_MS, which the test
  compares the budgets with.

Tests, both red before the fix:
- the node's own reading of the devnet listen environment must allow more
  reads a second than the drills make, for read (client and global) and
  health;
- a wait whose reads are refused with 429 must name the refusal when it
  times out.

Verified (run here):
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --file
  tests/devnet-stack-l1-origin.test.ts: 13 passed, 1 failed before; 14
  passed after.
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --file
  tests/devnet-stack-journey-robustness.test.ts: 22 passed, 1 failed
  before; 23 passed after.
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --related on the four changed
  sources: 777 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped in 72 files (the
  deployment-profile skips).
- tsc --noEmit in midgard-node-tools; eslint and prettier on the changed
  files; module-size ceilings.

Not verified:
- No passing acceptance run on a devnet stack yet. Whether 10 ms reads
  catch the 37 ms admission moment every time is not shown.

Bind every store to hubOraclePolicyId once at startup and drop redundant DA checks

Every persistent store now uses the single deployment identity defined in CONTEXT.md (hubOraclePolicyId) checked once at startup, failing closed on mismatch.

- da-committee-node: drop manifest_sha256, contract_deployment_info_sha256 and manifest_raw from committee_deployment, simplify initDeployment to write-once hubOraclePolicyId binding, drop the circular manifest re-hash in assertRetirementBinding, drop unused deploymentManifestRaw and contractDeploymentInfoSha256 from CommitteeConfig, and remove the per-/readyz getDeployment() query and 3-hash re-checks (deployment on /readyz is now { hubOraclePolicyId }).
- midgard-node-tools: drop the redundant storeMatchesConfigured check from committeeIsReady.
- midgard-watcher: store hub_oracle_policy_id in watcher_journal_schema and verify it once when opening watcher-journal.sqlite, failing closed with WatcherJournalConfigurationError before binding (even on an empty journal) without latching disk corruption.
- docs/public_testnet_readiness.md: replace the stale multi-field store-identity requirement with the single-identity startup rule and mark Store identity Done.

Record a node's snapshot anchor and give earlier events no row

A node that takes its ledger from a peer's snapshot of the confirmed head
holds what every event included by that head's block or an earlier one
did. This adds the record of that head and the rule that follows from it.
Nothing writes the record yet: the snapshot install does.

- `node_ledger_snapshot_anchor` (one row, written once): the confirmed
  header, its post-state UTxO root and its end time.
  `database/snapshot-anchor.ts` writes and reads it and holds the rule in
  its two forms, `includedByAnchor` and the SQL `includedAfterAnchor`.
- An event whose inclusion time is at or before the anchor's end time gets
  no row: deposits and withdrawals in `reconcileFollowerEvents`, forced
  orders in the forced-order hook. A block includes the events after its
  start time and at or before its end time, so these are exactly the
  events the anchor's block or an earlier one included.
- The commit horizon skips the same forced orders. A live order with no
  row bounds the horizon at its inclusion time minus one, which would have
  held every block after the anchor.

A node with no anchor row behaves as before.

Verified (rerun here):
- midgard-node tests/follower-events-snapshot-anchor.test.ts and
  tests/forced-orders-holds.test.ts: 6 passed.

Verified by the implementing run, not rerun here:
- Red before the rule: the deposit and the order at the anchor's end time
  each got a row (`expected [ …(2) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]`); with
  the ingest rule alone the horizon stayed bounded (`expected 4999 to be
  null`).
- Eight midgard-node event and forced-order test files: 74 passed.
  node-schema and reset-application-tables: 3 passed. tsc --noEmit for
  midgard-node; eslint and prettier on the changed files.

Not verified:
- The commit-worker and commit-anchor tests that read the horizon.
- Preflight.

Move the ledger-snapshot paging client into midgard-core

The watcher was the only client of the `ledger-snapshot` protocol. A node
starting from a peer's snapshot needs the same client, so the paging moves
next to the wire codec and the server's page reader, and the watcher calls
it.

- `fetchDaLedgerSnapshot` (`@al-ft/midgard-core/da-transport`) asks one
  peer for a root page by page and yields the entries in trie order. The
  caller supplies the function that sends one request and returns one
  response, and the transfer's abort signal. It asks for the next page only
  after the consumer took the current one, and checks nothing: the consumer
  (`LedgerStore.admit`) checks the stream against the root.
- `DaLedgerSnapshotUnserved` (the peer does not hold the root, rejected the
  request, or the request failed) and `DaLedgerSnapshotMalformed` replace
  the watcher's two error classes. The message texts are unchanged.
- The watcher keeps its request function (timeout, permit, admission,
  libp2p transport) in `ledger-snapshot-fetch.ts`.

The wire messages, the protocol id and the page size are unchanged.

Verified (rerun here):
- midgard-core tests/da-transport.ledger-snapshot.test.ts: 35 passed (9 new
  for the client).
- midgard-watcher ledger-snapshot-libp2p, ledger-snapshot-bootstrap and
  replayed-ledger.confirmed-chain tests: 17 passed, unchanged files.
- contrib mutate: removing the abort check and weakening the empty-page
  check are each caught by a test.
- tsc --noEmit for midgard-core, midgard-watcher, midgard-node,
  midgard-fault-proofs and midgard-node-tools; eslint and prettier on the
  changed files; contrib boundary --package midgard-watcher.

Not verified:
- The other test files of both packages, and preflight.

Delete the code that carried older database shapes, and the remaining labels

Every store is created whole from one schema, so nothing can hold a
row or a journal of an older shape.

- Withdrawal outref: every insert writes `decoded` or `undecodable`.
  The `unknown` state, its two indexes, the bounded backfill and the
  `E_PUBLIC_READ_MIGRATING` read refusal are gone.
- Availability operation journal: opening creates schema 3 or refuses
  another version. The in-place upgrade and its halt-cleared event are
  gone.
- Transaction fuzz: the reference leg runs on scripts naming the BLS
  builtins it used to skip, with no divergence, so the
  `blsTagNumbering` class and its pins are gone.
- The data-breadth wrapper script is gone; its seven tests run in the
  ordinary validation suite.
- Comments, test titles and messages state the rule instead of citing
  an issue number, goal label or ruling label.

Keep the tool when the acceptance journey attempts a submission

AcceptanceJourney overrides attempt to refuse work after cancellation. The
override still had the four parameters attempt had before 6e43bd7ed added
the tool, so it called the journey's attempt without it and every deposit
and withdrawal under acceptance defaulted to the node CLI. With the runner
fixed in the previous commit, an acceptance run on a fresh devnet stack
still stopped at deposits-concurrent with "error: unknown command
'deposit'" (campaign acceptance-user-cli-1, 2026-11-24).

The override now forwards whatever the journey's attempt takes, so a later
parameter cannot be dropped the same way.

Test: a deposit made through an AcceptanceJourney must reach the CLI runner
as the user tool. Before the fix it failed with "expected [ [ 'node',
'deposit' ] ] to deeply equal [ [ 'user', 'deposit' ] ]". The plain
journey's equivalent assertion never constructs the acceptance subclass.

Verified (run here):
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --file
  tests/devnet-stack-acceptance.test.ts: 18 passed, 1 failed before the
  fix; with tests/devnet-stack-acceptance-process.test.ts, 23 passed after.
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --related
  src/devnet-stack/acceptance-journey.ts: 775 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped
  in 72 files (the same deployment-profile skips as before).
- tsc --noEmit in midgard-node-tools; eslint and prettier on both files.

Not verified:
- No passing acceptance run on a devnet stack yet.

Run acceptance deposits and withdrawals through midgard-user

6e43bd7ed moved deposits and withdrawals to midgard-user and taught the
journey's own runner to honour a request's tool. The acceptance runner kept
its own copy of the launch and always ran the node CLI, so acceptance stopped
at its first journey phase with "error: unknown command 'deposit'".

Both runners now take the program, directory and environment from one
helper, cliProcess, and the run key from journeyRunKey; each keeps only its
own way of executing the process.

Test: a request naming the user tool, run through the acceptance runner
against stub CLIs, must start dist/cli.js in the user CLI package with the
user environment, the user's seed and the submission markers, and none of the
operator's secrets. Before the fix it failed with "expected 'node CLI' to be
'midgard-user'". A request naming no tool still runs the node CLI. It sits
beside the acceptance process tests because no existing test runs a request
through this runner.

Verified (run here):
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --file
  tests/devnet-stack-acceptance-process.test.ts: 3 passed, 1 failed before
  the fix; 4 passed after.
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --related on the three changed
  sources: 774 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped in 72 files (the skips are
  deployment-profile conditions in devnet-stack-watcher and
  devnet-stack-service-preflight).
- tsc --noEmit in midgard-node-tools; eslint and prettier on the four files.

Not verified:
- No acceptance run on a devnet stack.
